design.affected_system: public digital services, identity, applications, appointments, and assisted access
alternatives: compare eligible treated and credible untreated units for phased accessible digital and assisted-service redesign
estimate pre-specified overall and distributional effects of phased accessible digital and assisted-service redesign

assumptions: Page events, applications, errors, appointments, contacts, decisions, and outcomes remain distinct.
No automated score determines eligibility, enforcement, or denial without lawful human review.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
design.baseline: retain pre-intervention conditions for phased accessible digital and assisted-service redesign.

constraints.description: The digital public access and administrative service delivery evaluate must respect declared pre-specified assignment, comparison, outcome, spillover, and subgroup rules.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

design.decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
design.decision_owner: chief digital officer and administrative service delivery director
design.decision_question: Did phased redesign reduce verified completion friction without excluding non-digital users?
design.family_title: Digital public access and administrative service delivery

independence_key.binding_constraint: The digital public access and administrative service delivery evaluate must respect declared pre-specified assignment, comparison, outcome, spillover, and subgroup rules.
independence_key.decision_object: phased accessible digital and assisted-service redesign
independence_key.evidence_gate: Evidence for phased accessible digital and assisted-service redesign passes documented checks for dated assignment, comparison validity, pre-trends, outcome panels, attrition, spillovers, and falsification tests.
independence_key.intervention_mechanism: randomized encouragement or staggered service evaluation
independence_key.primary_outcome: change in verified eligible journey completion and user effort

design.intended_claim: A versioned evaluate design for comparing declared alternatives affecting phased accessible digital and assisted-service redesign, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: change in verified eligible journey completion and user effort
distributional gap in change in verified eligible journey completion and user effort
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not infer benefit receipt, well-being, or causal inclusion from page completion alone.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for phased accessible digital and assisted-service redesign passes documented checks for dated assignment, comparison validity, pre-trends, outcome panels, attrition, spillovers, and falsification tests.

design.title: Evaluate assisted digital service redesign
transportability_risks: Eligibility, identity, language, disability access, connectivity, trust, and service design differ.
Digital telemetry omits non-users and can encode device or tracking coverage.

family.affected_system: public digital services, identity, applications, appointments, and assisted access
claim_boundary: Service requests measure reported workload, not verified incidents, need, harm, or resolution.
Assignments and schedules are proposed operations, not completed work or public outcomes.
Design records do not establish agency adoption, deployment, productivity, or resident impact.
family.decision_owner: chief digital officer and administrative service delivery director
family.description: Eight decisions for journey diagnosis, channel forecasting, service redesign, assisted-access siting, support allocation, appointment scheduling, outage stress, and digital-service evaluation.
family.title: Digital public access and administrative service delivery

library_claim_boundary: The catalog contains 240 decision designs, not 240 city executions.
Exactly twelve designs map to existing Tier-D reference templates; 228 remain design-only.
A reference implementation can be an explicit negative release and does not imply impact.
No record claims a city binding, new method, deployment, adoption, or real-user outcome.
Future execution requires source binding, gate passage, and domain, legal, community, and operational review.
